It's not extremely bad, but it is certainly disappointing given how highly regarded this game and franchise appear to be. First things first: it is not, in any shape or form, an 'action adventure' game, as is often said. It is a third-person shooter of the most traditional kind there is: a succession of missions in various galactic settings, where you move from cover to cover, emptying your amo in the process, and very occasionally facing a boss. 
Perhaps its claim to 'adventure' status springs from its high number of cut-scenes or from the (decorative and minimal) option of chatting with your crew in the lobby between missions. Be that as it may, the scenario is lacklustre (loads of tired clichés, an incoherent villain, no psychological depth, etc.) and the dialogues are embarrassingly bad (filled nonsensical science-talk and 'Sir-Yes-Sir!' military jargon). The world-building itself is quite nice however, with some nice and detailed alien species. Unfortunately the repetitive missions only display the military element of each species, which are all pretty similar, only spiced up with some very generic clichés (i.e. the 'spiritual' asari are your elves, the krogans are your dwarves, etc.) The universe also seem to be filled with only young and sexy females, or young and sexy males either rugged or clueless. All in all it feels fairly puerile. 
So that's the 'adventure' element, now what about the action? Well it's not as bad: rhythm is good, weapons and power systems are nice, and the AI is usually pretty decent. However it is extremely repetitive (run to cover, shoot, move on is all you'll get) and the controls are sometimes badly thought out: I hope whatever marketing executive came up with 'let's use only one button to run, take cover, jump over the cover, and activate objects' was shot during playtest, because this is hands down the most annoying game mechanic I've ever encountered. With all that said, it is relaxing if not entertaining: I paid a tenner for it, and I don't regret it, but I really don't think it is worth a cent more.

Don't let my review full you; I've put way more than 60 hours into this game. This is simply the first play through after getting it on Steam. I love the series and the game is good, and by all means worth the price. Just it didn't deliver or finish as well as the two previous games in the series. There's more side banter, not just among the crew members than any of the series, and I feel the game has some of the most intense moments as well.....looking at you renegade run of Tuchanka. The weapons were a step up from 2 since I could see how choosing a different load out actually benefited me, and I wasn't overloaded on inventory maintenance like in 1. Squad maintenance is a lot like 2, and like two you can only level up those you are currently using; it doesn't really encourage trying other squad members if you have to stop at the beginning of the level and decide how to distribute their ability points since you haven't used them yet.  But yeah as the thumbs up shows its a must if you like RPG, Choices matter, Sci-fi, etc.
